headline: Pharmaceutical water matched to your dosage forms, and documented for every inspector who walks the plant
lead: Your dosage forms set the water grade: Purified Water (PW) for tablets, liquids and creams; Water for Injection (WFI) and pure steam for parenterals. Your markets set the inspectors: Health Canada under GUI-0001 and, for sterile products, GUI-0119 (in force since 1 April 2024), then the FDA and EU authorities if you export. We design, build and wet test systems that hold USP <645> 1.3 µS/cm at 25 °C, 500 ppb total organic carbon (TOC) and, for WFI, < 0.25 EU/mL endotoxin at the point of use, and we hand over the factory acceptance test (FAT) report and the installation and operational qualification (IQ/OQ) protocols an inspector asks for first.

blocks.h: The water system is the first utility an inspector walks
body: Water is the excipient most drug products use most, the final rinse of almost every cleaning cycle and the feed to every WFI still and pure steam generator. An inspection of a water system reads the design, the qualification and the trend data together: slopes and dead legs on the drawings, the sanitization record, the alert and action levels and what was done when one was crossed.

Most of the water findings we are asked to fix were set at design: a loop with no spare capacity for the next product line, a point of use added without a drawing update, a qualification file with no weld records, an endotoxin target for a WFI still that nobody wrote down. We start from your products, your markets and your expansion plan, then choose the systems and write the records that answer those questions before an inspector asks them.

We work for innovator and generic drug manufacturers, natural health product (NHP) makers and contract manufacturers in Canada, on oral solid dose (OSD), non-sterile liquid and semi-solid, and sterile and parenteral lines.

body: Source: EMA Guideline on the quality of water for pharmaceutical use (EMA/CHMP/CVMP/QWP/496873/2018), in effect since 1 February 2021. USP publishes no equivalent table; for a Canadian or US product the grade is the one stated in your registration and specification. The guideline sets minimums. Your product file and risk assessment can set a higher grade, never a lower one.

blocks.h: What each inspector reads, and where we answer it
cols: What they read on the water system
rows: Health Canada, all drug establishments

GUI-0001 interprets Part C, Division 2 of the Food and Drug Regulations: premises, equipment, sanitation, validation and records. For water, that means design, qualification, maintenance, calibration and trend review
Health Canada, sterile products

GUI-0119, Health Canada's adoption of EU GMP Annex 1 (2022): WFI route (6.10), no dead legs and drainable slopes (6.7), turbulent flow (6.9), vent filters (6.11), sanitization schedule (6.12), continuous TOC and conductivity on WFI (6.15) and pure steam (6.17), all inside your contamination control strategy
FDA, sites shipping to the United States

21 CFR Part 211: equipment design (211.63), cleaning and maintenance (211.67), automatic equipment and records (211.68). Investigators work from the FDA Guide to Inspections of High Purity Water Systems: dead legs, sanitization, sampling and a full year of data
EU authorities and importers

Ph. Eur. monographs on every attribute, the EMA water guideline and Annex 15 qualification. Membrane WFI needs notice to the GMP supervisory authority before use. The Canada–EU mutual recognition agreement (MRA) on GMP covers many drug products; your regulatory team confirms the scope for yours
Health Canada, natural health products

GUI-0158 version 4 (in force 4 March 2026): potable water as the minimum, purification, storage and distribution equipment operated to give water of appropriate chemical and microbiological purity, and water test records kept

blocks.h: How the systems connect in a pharmaceutical plant
blocks.caption: An oral solid dose or liquids plant usually stops at the PW loop. A sterile plant also feeds PW to a WFI still or membrane WFI skid and to a pure steam generator, which serves autoclaves and SIP directly. So the PW system is sized for its own points of use plus that feed demand, and designed to the still's and generator's feed limits. Pretreatment keeps chlorine, chloramine and scale off the membranes through Canadian winter and summer feed water. Monitoring and controls run across all of it, with audit-trailed records under 21 CFR Part 11 and EU GMP Annex 11.

blocks.h: Decisions to settle before the URS is approved

items.t: Product mix now and in five years
items.d: A generics site that adds a liquid line or a sterile suite needs more PW, or a WFI feed, from the same generator. We size headers and generator capacity for the plan you can see and write the expansion into the user requirement specification (URS).
USP stage 1 conductivity is the tighter value for PW; Ph. Eur. adds nitrates and its own microbial method. Designing to both costs little at the start and a lot to add after qualification.

Both routes are pharmacopoeial in USP and Ph. Eur. Distillation fills a hot loop and has the longer record with inspectors. Membrane WFI uses less energy and needs a stronger control strategy and, for EU markets, a notice to the supervisory authority.

Hot circulation above 70 °C is the example Annex 1 gives for WFI. PW loops are often ambient with periodic hot water or ozone sanitization. The choice sets energy use, point-of-use cooling and the sanitization record you keep.

Feed temperature can swing from near freezing in winter to over 20 °C in summer, and some municipal supplies use chloramine. We size membranes at your coldest month and design chloramine removal and carbon dioxide control together.

Duplex generation trains and isolable loop sections let you sanitize, service or tie in new points of use without stopping every line. We plan tie-ins around your shutdown calendar and change control.

blocks.h: Questions engineering, validation and QA leads ask

items.q: Do we need WFI if all our products are non-sterile?
items.a: Usually not. The EMA guideline sets PW as the minimum for oral, cutaneous, nasal, ear, rectal and vaginal products and for granulation and coating. The exceptions are products that must be sterile and non-pyrogenic, such as some nebuliser solutions. Your product registration and specification decide.

items.q: Can one system supply products for Canada, the United States and Europe?
items.a: Yes. We design to the stricter of USP and Ph. Eur. on each attribute, test both at FAT where the methods allow it, and write both into the functional specification, so the same records answer Health Canada, the FDA and an EU importer.

items.q: Is membrane WFI acceptable to Health Canada and the FDA?
items.a: USP allows WFI by distillation or a purification process shown to be equivalent or superior to it, and Ph. Eur. 0169 has allowed reverse osmosis with other techniques since April 2017. Health Canada applies the pharmacopoeia named in your product file. For EU markets, notice goes to the GMP supervisory authority before use. Confirm the route with your regulatory team product by product; the WFI by membrane page sets out the control strategy.

items.q: We make natural health products. Do we need USP Purified Water?
items.a: GUI-0158 sets potable water as the minimum. Many NHP makers move to PW for liquids, for products whose specification names a pharmacopoeial grade, or when microbial results over shelf life call for it. A PW skid on the same platform as a drug-grade system can be qualified to the level your product needs.

items.q: We are adding a production line. Must the whole water system be requalified?
items.a: Not normally. The change goes through your change control, and a risk assessment sets the qualification scope: usually IQ and OQ for the new section and a period of increased sampling at the new points of use. We state that scope before the first cut and plan the tie-in around your shutdown.

items.q: Can we use the water during PQ?
items.a: WHO TRS 1033 Annex 3 allows use in phase 2 of PQ with quality unit approval, after a first phase of at least two weeks with no manufacturing use. Your validation master plan decides. The commissioning and qualification page sets out each phase.
